description:
Step 1 of 3: call it until ready_to_quote is true, sending back the collected it returns each time and each answer under answer_as.key. Then start_quote.

Returns the one question to put to the customer now, in their language, with the options to offer when the field has a fixed set. Call it before each question and again after every answer, until `ready_to_quote` is true, then call `start_quote`.

Send only what the customer said this turn, in `answered`, together with the `collected` from the last call. The connector keeps the record of the conversation, so nothing is repeated and an answer given before its turn is not lost. When `ready_to_quote` turns true, `summary` is what the customer has said: read it back and let them correct it before quoting.

It exists so the order and the pace are the connector's rather than a matter of judgement: Sigo's customers are working people, often quoting on a phone, and a turn that asks for four things at once is where they give up.

Once a ZIP is given it is checked here, so a customer outside the states Sigo is licensed in is told before being walked through the rest.

There are two stretches. `stage: "first_quote"` is the one that ends in estimates. `stage: "second_round"` is for a customer who saw those estimates and wants to finish the application so the carrier can quote it for real: it asks where the car is kept, the VIN, who owns it, the licence, and a few more. The prices it leads to are still estimates; the final quote comes after the carrier's own questions, in Sigo's link. `get_quote` says when that is worth offering.

A vehicle a business uses for its work is commercial auto and is not quoted here: use commercial_next_question. Someone who drives only for apps like Uber or DoorDash stays here.

answered.description: Only what the customer said this turn. Everything from earlier turns is already in `collected` and must not be repeated here.

address.description: Second round. Where the car is kept.

document_number_settled.description: Second round. Send once every driver who is not excluded has given their document's number.

document_settled.description: Send once the identity document is settled, including a customer who gave none.

document_type.description: Which of the six it is, sent with `document_settled`, so the summary can read it back. Never the number: that goes to `start_quote` only.

driver_name.description: The name, sent with `driver_named`, so the summary can read it back.

driver_named.description: Send once the driver's name is known.

household_drivers.description: Second round. The others in the home by name, sent with `household_drivers_settled`; an empty list when there is nobody. Read back in the summary.

household_drivers_settled.description: Second round. Send once the household has been asked about, whoever the answer added.

lienholder_settled.description: Second round. Send once the loan holder is settled.

marital_status.description: Sending `married` is what brings up the spouse.

ownership.description: Second round. Sending `financed` or `leased` is what brings up the lienholder.

primary_driver_settled.description: Send once who drives the car most is settled.

prior_coverage_settled.description: Second round. Send once both the months covered and the expiry are known.

spouse_named.description: Send once the spouse is on the quote.

vehicle.description: The car as the customer gave it, sent with `vehicle_described`. It settles nothing on its own; it is what the summary reads back.

vehicle_described.description: Send once year, make and model are all known.

vin.description: Second round. The VIN as the customer gave it, so the summary can read it back.

vin_settled.description: Second round. Send once every vehicle has its VIN.

zip_code.description: The ZIP code, exactly as the customer gave it.

collected.description: The `collected` from the previous call. Leave it out on the first question of a conversation and send it on every call after that: it carries everything answered so far, so nothing has to be repeated and nothing is lost.

locale.description: The language the customer is writing in. Set it from their own messages rather than leaving the default: the estimate's notice comes back in this language, and a notice the customer cannot read discloses nothing. Sigo serves these two languages only.

stage.description: Which stretch the conversation is in. `second_round` is for a customer who saw prices and wants to finish the application; it asks a different set, and the prices it leads to are still estimates.

name: next_question

key.description: The exact key to send this answer under in `answered` on the next call.

type.description: The value's shape. `mark` means send `true` once the matter is settled; the details themselves (a name, a VIN, a spouse) go to start_quote, not here.

values.description: For `enum`: the only values accepted, in English.

answer_as.description: How to send the answer back. Null on the closing step, when there is nothing left to answer.

ask.description: The question, ready to put to the customer, in their language.

collected.description: Everything answered so far, this turn included. Send it back on the next call. It is the connector's record of the conversation, so nothing has to be asked twice.

field.description: The question being asked, by name. Not the key to answer under: that is `answer_as.key`.

options.description: Every choice the customer may pick, when the field has a fixed set.

ready_to_quote.description: True when nothing is missing and start_quote can be called.

summary.description: What the customer has answered, to read back to them for confirmation. Present only once `ready_to_quote` is true; null while there are still questions to ask.

title: The next thing to ask the customer
